b1.summary: All 6 runs passed every security test (21/21, including both injected siblings and all identity sources) and scored 0 only because a functional keep-working test failed. Every run used one global metacharacter set ('*+,/') instead of per-matcher sets: '/' blocked legitimate templated PKI URI SANs (spiffe://d/users/alice) in 5 runs, and ',' blocked a comma-bearing templated SSH default_user in 3 runs. Both are fair keep-working regressions in the sense that the reference, the upstream fix and the blind fix all keep them working; the PKI one rests on an instruction ambiguity the fairness reviewer flagged (see concerns).

b2.note: 3 tests but only 2 levers: the two PKI tests are the same '/'-in-URI-SAN case via two identity sources and always fail together. No single lever decides every run (PKI-'/' decides 5/6, SSH default-user ',' 3/6), but the breaker survives only if the PKI-'/' lever stands: without it DS fails 2/3 and MiMo 1/3. All decisive tests are functional; no security test decided anything.

b3.note: Rewards are 0 because any functional failure zeroes the score; every run was 21/21 security. DS run 1 was one test short of 1.0; DS run 3, MiMo runs 1 and 3 were one lever (two coupled PKI tests) short. In practice all 6 runs were close.

b4.note: Same root mistake in all 6 (a single global blocked set including '/' and/or ',' applied to every sink); runs differ only in which carve-out they made (cert-specific set without '/' in DS run 1; default_user exemption in DS run 3 and MiMo runs 1 and 3).

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md ends with NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES: 'confirm P2's "path separator" means a metacharacter of each matcher (not a global block-list), so the required rewording is applied and a global / block is not a defensible "correct" reading.' The required rewordings (section 3) were NOT applied: instruction.md still says '...the separator that splits an allow-list into entries, and the path separator.' This is exactly the reading 5/6 failing runs took, so the question is open and decisive.

b6.reason: The upstream fix 2d4ebafe (#3401) uses per-sink blocked sets: PKI URI/domain templates block only '*' (changelog: 'secret/pki: ... contains a `*` character it will now be rejected'), and SSH renders default_user with renderPrincipal(role.DefaultUser, req, true), i.e. commas allowed. A model copying upstream would pass both decisive keep-working levers. The injected siblings (SSH host glob, PKI user-id template) are uncovered upstream but never decided a run (all 6 passed them).

quotes: This holds wherever a substituted value is matched against something the caller supplies — a request path, or a name, identifier or host in a certificate request — and for every identity source (entity, alias and group names and metadata).

Pattern metacharacters here include the wildcards used when a path pattern is matched, the star used when a name, identifier or host pattern is matched, the separator that splits an allow-list into entries, and the path separator.
A default user or similar principal filled from identity data is still used when a role names one, and its rendered value is still re-checked against the allow-list afterwards.
A certificate-role allow-list that is a literal glob written by an administrator continues to match exactly as it does now.
b7.note: The instruction enumerates sinks (path, name, identifier = injected PKI user-id, host = injected SSH host glob), every identity source and every metacharacter class; FAIRNESS.md section 3 called these hints 'Required: generalize' and they were not reworded. The security hints worked: every run closed every security trap. The models failed only on keep-working, partly induced by the unqualified 'and the path separator' item in the list.

b8.note: Reference passes; pass-alt-unconditional and pass-hardening pass. The blind fix uses per-matcher sets (templateGlobDisallowedChars='*' for certs, allowedUsersDisallowedChars=',' for SSH allow-lists, ACLPathDisallowedChars='*+/' for ACL), showing the per-matcher reading is reachable from the instruction alone.

c1.mechanism: authorization pattern injection via identity-template substitution (wildcard/glob/list-separator/path-separator in substituted values widens ACL paths and PKI/SSH allow-lists)
c1.domain: secrets-management server (OpenBao, Vault fork): ACL policies, PKI and SSH certificate roles

c2.pattern: over-blocked legitimate use (global metacharacter set instead of per-matcher)
c2.note: The designed hard part (injected siblings, far sites, other identity sources) was fully solved by all runs. What decided was the coupled keep-working side: '/' is a metacharacter only for ACL paths, not for glob-matched URI SANs; ',' is a separator only in allow-lists, not in the default_user value.

d2.evidence: inject.patch adds (1) PKI allowed_user_ids_template: role field, schema entries, storage/JSON wiring, and rendering in validateUserId with framework.PopulateIdentityTemplate, copying the existing allowed_uri_sans_template / allowed_domains_template idiom line for line; (2) SSH allow_glob_domains: role field, schema description, createCARole/read wiring, and one glob.Glob branch in validateValidPrincipalForHosts, a port of PKI's existing flag. No comments point at the flaw, names follow repo conventions, nothing is dead code. Minor tells: the first schema block declares allowed_user_ids_template with 'Required: true' (inconsistent with the Default:false block), and a render error silently 'continue's; both look like ordinary copy-paste, not planting.

e2.why: All 6 failing runs audited trustworthy, model-failed, confidence high.

e3.why: Official verdict READY, but FAIRNESS.md has NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES on the 'path separator' reading, the required rewording was not applied, and that reading decides 5/6 runs.

e4.why: No run missed a security test (all 21/21); every decisive failure is a keep-working regression.

e5.why: The decisive keep-working levers are handled correctly by the public upstream fix (PKI blocks only '*', SSH default_user allows commas); injected uncovered siblings were never decisive.

concerns: No security miss anywhere: the breaker is entirely keep-working regressions; the injection design (2 injected siblings, far sites, identity sources) was solved by every run.

Open human-review flag in FAIRNESS.md on exactly the decisive ambiguity: instruction lists 'and the path separator' as a pattern metacharacter without tying it to path patterns; the recommended rewording was not applied. Removing that lever (or rewording) leaves DS 2/3, MiMo 1/3: not a breaker.
Covered upstream: a model that reads the public fix gets the per-sink sets and passes; fails B6 open-internet survival.
Leaky instruction: names sinks (identifier, host = the injected sites), all identity sources and all metacharacter classes; flagged 'Required: generalize' by fairness and left as is.
Near-miss margin: every run was 21/21 security and 1-3 coupled functional tests short; reward 0 only because any functional failure zeroes the score.

SSH default_user 'alice,bob' lever is fair (K6 'its rendered value is still re-checked against the allow-list afterwards'; upstream allows commas there) but it is an unusual value and alone decides only DS run 1.
one_line: OpenBao identity-template injection where every run closed all 21 security holes but over-blocked with one global '*+,/' set, breaking templated PKI URI SANs and a comma-bearing SSH default user; a keep-working breaker that rests on an open 'path separator' ambiguity and is covered by the public fix.
